vulnerability_patterns.description: A length derived from an input note name field controls a numeric decode loop without first being bounded to the capacity of the destination integer. Oversized bytes values let untrusted name data continue through shift-based numeric accumulation beyond the intended value width. The patch blocks this by checking bytes against sizeof (val), reporting a corrupt name field, and returning FALSE before the loop.
trigger_conditions: bytes is derived from pnote->namesz - (name - pnote->namedata)
bytes controls while (bytes --) in the GNU_BUILD_ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_NUMERIC case
the loop consumes *name++ and shifts/accumulates bytes into val
there is no preceding guard equivalent to if (bytes > sizeof (val)) return FALSE
fix_patterns: change val from unsigned long to unsigned long long to match the intended numeric print width
add if (bytes > sizeof (val)) as a barrier before the decode loop
on oversized bytes, call error(...) and return FALSE instead of continuing to parse
keep printf format specifiers consistent with the widened val type

shared_analysis.analysis_rationale: The patch computes bytes from pnote->namesz and the current name offset, then adds an explicit upper bound check before a byte-consuming numeric decode loop. Before the patch, bytes could exceed the storage width of val and still drive while (bytes --), causing repeated shifts/accumulation into a too-small numeric value. The fix widens val to unsigned long long and returns FALSE when bytes > sizeof (val), directly blocking oversized name fields from reaching the decode loop.
